Update: `Router.navigate` doesn't work either. E.g. the following doesn't work:

```ts
this.router.navigate(["/profile", { outlets: { sidebar: null } }]);
```

Workaround: add a click handler and call navigate a second time, **but** only after the first one completes.

```ts
this.router.navigate(["/profile"]).then(() =>
            this.router.navigate([".", { outlets: { sidebar: null } }]));
```
Please provide a quick repro. Thanks.

Created a new project with the latest cli and then added the components as explained above. Please take a look: https://github.com/tinchou/router-repro.

-------

EDIT

Just tried to use `ng github-pages:deploy` but it fails trying to run `git rm -r`. Anyway, I copied the contents from `/dist` and deployed them manually, and here's a live demo!

https://tinchou.github.io/router-repro/

In the vsavkin's book, he says : 

`We can also remove segments by setting them to ‘null’.

router.navigate([{outlets: {popup: null}}])`

But he never set a path and a outlet. In this case, we can use 

<a [routerLink]="[{outlets: {primary: 'profile',sidebar: null}}]">

If it can help

@WilliamKoza it seems to work using the `primary` outlet.  Now I found it in [the docs](https://angular.io/docs/ts/latest/guide/router.html) and it makes sense:

> `outlet`: The name of the `RouterOutlet` used to render the route. For an unnamed outlet, the outlet name is **primary**.

This works perfect for me, thanks a lot (but I believe the issue still stands).

Just one gotcha: in my real application it only works if specifying an empty string as the first parameter `<a [routerLink]="['', {outlets: {primary: 'profile', sidebar: null}}]">`

same issue here. i try to close the a modal window. I have a outlet called "modal" and there i load my modal window component. If i want to close it (without knowing where i'm) with modal: null it routes to the modal again.

same issue. i have a named outlet call popup, just like in the docs. when i try to close it with:
`this.router.navigate([{ outlets: {popup: null }}]);`
It just does nothing.

Also, if I try to use `"../"` as the first portion - `this.router.navigate( "../" ... )`, then the secondary outlet *does close*; however, it leaves it in the URL as `//inbox:)`. And, at that point, if I refresh the browser page, I get an error that the primary route can no longer match.

For what it's worth, I was able to get this working by using the **parent component's** `ActivatedRoute` instance (`this.activatedRoute.parent`) in the `router.navigate()` method. I [wrote up my approach here](https://www.bennadel.com/blog/3351-closing-secondary-router-outlet-views-from-within-the-named-route-view-components-in-angular-4-4-4.htm).

@challe my pleasure :) It's a _partial solution_. It still basically means the `[routerLinker]` can't change a secondary outlet that it doesn't own; which is unfortunate because it means that you can't have natural HREF values (and that you have to create special methods in those cases). I think this might end up being a significant blocker for me :|
